_: The tom's free parameters against the module's own recordings. Eleven knobs, not the seventy-one `--spec auto` offers a drum note, because a kit note is ONE cell: the module holds one recording per piece at one velocity, so an automatic spec fits seventy-one values to a single measurement and reproduces the recording rather than the drum.
_pinned: Everything the module states outright is absent here and must stay absent. `base_freq_hz`, `head_diameter_m`, `shell_depth_m`, `air_spring`, `mode_decay_s`, `pitch_drop` and `pitch_drop_ms` are read off the reference's own measured row - a frequency, a geometry, a measured axisymmetric split, a measured band decay, a measured descending strike. Offering a measured quantity to a search replaces a measurement with a fit, and the search will take it.
_transfer: Fitted on note 45 and read as a law rather than as one drum's settings: the six toms differ in the pinned columns and share these. The other five keys are the held-out set - adopt a value only if `compare` improves on them too, since a knob that helps 45 alone is fitting 45's recording.
_weights: `level` is weighted here, where most voices leave it at zero. A kit's members are only as right as they are against each other, and a search free to lose energy will: the toms' own spread across the family is 7.8 dB in the module and the voice's radiation alone produces 3.

knobs._: Where the stick lands, as a fraction of the radius. Below a third the m >= 1 modes the drum's pitch is heard in are barely excited; at the rim the fundamental goes instead.
Contact time. It is the low-pass the stick itself is: a mode at f keeps |sinc(f*tau)/(1-(f*tau)^2)| of the strike, so this alone sets how far up the series the hit reaches.
How much shorter the contact gets as the stick is swung harder.
How fast damping rises with frequency. Measured near a half on all six toms; searched around that rather than pinned, because it is read off octave bands that hold several modes each.
The dense region above the modes the engine can place, which a membrane has and twelve resonators cannot reach.
The stick's own radiation, which reaches the listener without passing through the voice's filter or envelope. It is the first millisecond and nothing after it.
The shell, which is a body the head drives rather than a layer of its own.

The upper bound on what the noise band radiates. A head is a poor radiator well before the band the strike fills runs out, and without this the dense region arrives at full level all the way to Nyquist - which is most of the brightness the model carries over the module.
